name: Richard L. Weiner
headline: Orthopaedic surgeon, hip and knee replacement
on_the_show: Dr. Weiner, who has worked alongside Dave since 1990, spent much of the hour on how to keep people out of the operating room. He described a ladder of care that starts with conservative treatment and physical therapy and treats surgery as the last resort. On knee replacement, he puts it at over 40% of total knee patients who could have had a partial instead, against about 10% in the United States who actually get one, and he explained why a partial can feel more like a normal knee.
on_the_show_quote: You don’t treat an X-ray, you treat the patient.

background.text: He earned a Bachelor of Science in chemical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science, then his medical degree from the University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine.
He completed his orthopaedic surgery residency at New Jersey Medical School, University of Medicine and Dentistry of New Jersey, in 1991.
He is a Diplomate of the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery and a Fellow of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.
At St. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach he served as Chief of Orthopedic Trauma Surgery from 1993 to 2019.
His practice profile notes that he uses the Oxford partial knee replacement and dual mobility total hip replacements.
